page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
steps.why: The gene for the ancestral organ is still present, so it can occasionally be expressed again.
common_mistakes: Defining atavism as any birth defect. It is the return of a vestigial organ.
steps.memory_tip: An old ancestral feature reappearing well developed.
steps.margin_note: The word vestigial carries the mark.
lines: Atavism is the sudden reappearance of some
vestigial organs in a better developed

steps.label: An example
steps.why: The human tail bone is a vestige, and very rarely a baby is born with the tail itself.
common_mistakes: Giving a vestigial organ as the example. The example must be one that REAPPEARED.
steps.memory_tip: A baby born with a tail is the standard example.

lines.text: Example: a human baby born with a tail

insider_note: The word 'vestigial' must appear. Atavism is a vestigial organ coming back, not just any unusual feature.
